name: Cross-Domain Dependency Map
method: Imports were parsed for every class in app/ and grouped by area, then each cross-area edge was inspected for its actual purpose before being classified. A dependency was not classified as a violation without reading what it is used for.

classifications.application-mediated: crosses via an Application use case that owns the boundary
classifications.suspicious: violates or strains a stated rule and needs a decision

dangerous_relationships_checked.evidence: Booking depends on Pricing one-directionally; CampaignPricingEngine imports no Booking class.
Payment transitions Booking status; Booking imports no Payment class.
One-directional: Financial reads booking projections and owns commissions.
Reporting performs reads only; no reverse edge exists.
Resolved in Phase 0.13. User::hasPermission was the sole instance and now depends on app/Support/Authorization instead.
No Domain class imports an SDK, HTTP client, Mail or Storage facade.
No Domain class imports anything under App\Http.

edges.evidence: Booking -> InventoryService, BookingCapacityService via constructor injection in CreateCampaignBookingUseCase / RescheduleBookingUseCase / CheckBookingAvailabilityQuery
edges.note: Availability is a subordinate capability of booking; dependency is one-directional and declared.
Pricing is called, never the reverse.
Booking does not call revenue allocation directly; it calls the application use case that owns it.
Storage access is behind StorageContractInterface since Phase 0.12.
Point debit is a financial side effect invoked explicitly by the use case, not implicitly by the model.

edges.evidence: app/Models/Booking.php:41-90 - updated/deleting model events call app(LoyaltyService), app(SettingsService), app(ReferralTrackingService)
edges.note: A persistence model is driving three cross-domain side effects through the service locator. Highest-risk architectural item found in Phase 0.13. Left in place: the side effects are load-bearing financial logic and relocating them would change transaction timing.
Payment transitions booking status; Booking does not depend on Payment.
Commission accrual is owned by Financial and called by Payment-adjacent flows.
Gateway SDK is confined to Infrastructure per Rule 3.
Financial reads booking projections; no write-back into Booking rules.
Commission ledger is the contract between Financial and Partner.

edges.evidence: app/Application/Reporting/Queries/* -> DB::table read of persisted booking_screens splits and partner_commissions
edges.note: Reporting consumes STORED financial truth; it never recomputes it. This is the canonical pattern and is the reason the two commission totals in the referral report legitimately differ.

edges.evidence: zero write calls anywhere under app/Application/Reporting
edges.note: Verified: the reporting layer performs no writes. Reporting -> transactional mutation is the explicitly prohibited edge and it does not exist.

edges.evidence: app/Domain/Pricing/CampaignPricingEngine.php imports 7 App\Services classes including LoyaltyService and PricingRuleEngine
edges.note: A Domain engine depends on legacy Services. Genuine Rule 3 / Rule 9 pressure. Not remediated in this phase - see the debt register.
Domain engine reads persisted settings; Rule 9 requires pricing determinism for identical parameters, and a DB-backed setting is an external input to the calculation.

edges.evidence: PartnerService -> PartnerApproved/PartnerRejected events; booking rows carry created_by_partner_id
edges.note: Partner ownership of bookings is recorded, not computed cross-domain.
Provider owns screen assets.

edges.evidence: Booking media approval/rejection -> events -> NotificationEventSubscriber -> NotificationService
edges.note: Event-mediated, not a direct call.
Since Phase 0.12 no direct Mail facade usage remains outside the adapter.
Phase 0.13: the dependency direction is now Support <- {Http, Models} rather than Models -> Http.

edges.evidence: Api/ProfileController, Auth controllers read the authenticated user from the request
edges.note: Unavoidable for an HTTP adapter; noted rather than flagged as a defect.
